user.description: Choose a badge to set up. Only badges that are advertising are listed: put the badge in BT-PAIRING mode first.

data_description.address: Badges seen by Home Assistant's Bluetooth adapters and proxies.

bluetooth_confirm.description: Set up {name}? Home Assistant connects to the badge once to read its model and firmware, so keep it in BT-PAIRING mode until setup finishes.

error.cannot_connect: Could not connect to the badge. Make sure it is in BT-PAIRING mode and no phone is connected to it, then try again.

abort.no_devices_found: No advertising badges found. Put the badge in BT-PAIRING mode and try again.

data.set_clock: Set the badge clock on upload

data_description.font: Font for text sent by the Message, notify and send_messages entities and actions.
data_description.mode: Mode for send_messages messages that do not set one, and the initial Mode entity value.
data_description.speed: Speed for send_messages messages that do not set one, and the initial Speed entity value.
data_description.flash: Flash for send_messages messages that do not set it, and the initial Flash entity value.
data_description.marquee: Marquee for send_messages messages that do not set it, and the initial Marquee entity value.
data_description.set_clock: Every upload carries the current time, which the open firmware loads into its clock.
data_description.wide_text: In fixed, snowflake, picture and laser modes the badge shows text wider than 44 pixels one 44-pixel page at a time. Choose to keep that, scroll the text instead, or show only the first page.
data_description.keep_bluetooth_on: Stay connected for 2.5 seconds after each upload. The open firmware switches Bluetooth off 1.5 seconds after an upload but turns it back on when Home Assistant disconnects, so the badge stays reachable. Not yet verified on hardware.

options.page: Show it a page at a time (badge default)

options.auto: Scroll if wider than the display

not_advertising.message: {name} is not advertising over Bluetooth. Put the badge in BT-PAIRING mode, or enable always-on Bluetooth on it, then try again.

cannot_connect.message: Could not connect to {name}: {error}. Put the badge in BT-PAIRING mode, or enable always-on Bluetooth on it, then try again.

pin_required.message: The badge has security enabled. Enter BT-PAIRING mode and pass the PIN it shows to the send_messages action.

pin_rejected.message: The badge rejected the PIN. The PIN changes every time the badge enters BT-PAIRING mode.

path_not_allowed.message: Home Assistant is not allowed to read {path}. Add its folder to allowlist_external_dirs.

media_not_local.message: {path} is not a local media file; only local media can be sent to the badge.

nextgen_required.message: {name} does not support this: it needs the open Badge Magic firmware.

invalid_name.message: The Bluetooth name must be 1 to 20 bytes long.

splash_too_large.message: The splash image {path} is {width}x{height} pixels, which takes {bytes} bytes; the badge accepts at most {max} bytes (for example 48x42 or 40x44).

send_messages.name: Send messages
send_messages.description: Uploads up to 8 messages to the badge, replacing everything stored on it. Each message has either text or an image. On the open firmware the badge then returns to its menu.

messages.name: Messages
messages.description: List of 1 to 8 messages. Each has 'text' or 'image' (a file path Home Assistant may read, or a local media-source:// URI), and optionally 'mode' (scroll_left, scroll_right, scroll_up, scroll_down, fixed, animation, snowflake, picture, laser), 'speed' (1-8), 'flash', 'marquee' and 'font' (normal, compact, tiny). Fields left out use the badge's options.

pin.name: PIN
pin.description: The 4-digit PIN the badge shows in BT-PAIRING mode when its security setting is on.

set_clock.name: Set clock
set_clock.description: Send the current time so the badge sets its clock. Defaults to the badge's option.

set_splash_screen.name: Set splash screen
set_splash_screen.description: Replaces the image the badge scrolls through when it starts (open firmware). Takes effect at the next start.

image.name: Image
image.description: An image file or .xbm file Home Assistant may read, or a local media-source:// URI. Larger images are scaled down to fit 48x44 pixels; the bitmap must fit in 255 bytes.

frame_height.name: Frame height
frame_height.description: Rows the splash moves per step.

stream_frame.name: Stream frame
stream_frame.description: Shows one 44x11 frame on the display right away (open firmware). Turns streaming on if needed; the badge's own messages return when streaming is turned off.

text.name: Text
text.description: Text to show. Give text or an image.

image.name: Image
image.description: An image file Home Assistant may read, or a local media-source:// URI, scaled to 11 pixels high.

font.name: Font
font.description: Font for the text. Defaults to the badge's option.

align.name: Alignment
align.description: Where to place content narrower than the display.

stream_text.name: Stream text
stream_text.description: Shows text by streaming frames to the display (open firmware), with Home Assistant doing the scrolling. Returns once streaming has started.

font.name: Font
font.description: Font for the text. Defaults to the badge's option.

effect.name: Effect
effect.description: Scroll the text, show it fixed, or scroll only if it is wider than the display.

fps.name: Frames per second
fps.description: Scroll speed: one column per frame.

duration.name: Duration
duration.description: Keep scrolling (or showing fixed text) for this many seconds. Without it, scrolling text passes once.

stop_after.name: Stop streaming when done
stop_after.description: Leave streaming afterwards so the badge's own messages return. Otherwise the last frame stays on the display.

bluetooth_off_after_upload.title: {name} switched Bluetooth off after an upload
bluetooth_off_after_upload.description:
The open Badge Magic firmware turns Bluetooth off after it receives messages, so Home Assistant can no longer reach {name}. Put the badge in BT-PAIRING mode to reconnect.

To keep the badge reachable, turn on **Keep Bluetooth on after uploads** in the badge's options, and turn on the **Always-on Bluetooth** switch so the badge advertises after it restarts. This issue clears itself when the badge advertises again.
